newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank to close some Belgian branch offices.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank to close some Belgian branch offices.

text.p: Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, plans to close some branch offices in the coming years, a bank spokesman said on Friday.

He declined to confirm or deny a report on BRTN radio which said the bank planned to close 80 of its 1,100 branch offices in the next three years. The radio said the closures would focus on the big cities, where there was an excess of bank offices.
"Some offices will be closed, there will be a reorganisation, but we can give no precise figure," he said.
Spokeswoman Kathleen Steels told BRTN radio that there would be no job cuts.
"The people will be employed in more specialised sectors of activities. Some will go work in other, bigger branch offices," she said.
A Generale Bank union spokesman told the radio he was still worried by the move, which he saw as a preparation for a possible merger with Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL).
A merger between the two has been discussed publicly for months, but remains blocked by opposition from Dutch BBL shareholder Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING).
Belgium is one of Europe's most overbanked countries. Most towns and villages have more bank branch offices than bakeries.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
